slides.title: Circuit breaker vs **rate limiter**. What's the difference?
slides.text: One is a quota. One is a failure detector 👉

slides.title: A **quota** on traffic
bullets: 📏|Caps requests per window, per user / IP / key

slides.title: A **failure detector**
bullets: 🩺|Watches failures and latency of a dependency

cols.title: 📏 Rate limit
cols.text: Trigger: request count. Protects the service. Response: 429.

cols.title: 🔌 Breaker
cols.text: Trigger: failures / slowness. Protects the caller. Response: fast error or fallback.

slides.title: Cache down? **Layer them**
bullets: 📏|Rate limit caps total and per-client load
🔌|Breaker opens when the DB times out

slides.title: Common **traps**
bullets: 🕳️|Breaker with no fallback: just fast errors
🌐|Per-IP limits behind NAT hit many users

slides.title: Say this in 1 line
slides.text: **Rate limiting** is proactive and caps traffic by policy (429). A **circuit breaker** is reactive: it opens when a dependency fails, **fails fast**, then **half-opens** to probe recovery. Use **both**.

slides.text: Fixed window, sliding window, token bucket. Follow and save 🔖
